cohort: 196 asphyxiated newborns admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of a tertiary care Military Hospital in Pakistan from December 1, 2012 to December 1, 2013
finding: Several perinatal factors, including cesarean section, prolonged second stage of labor, prolonged rupture of membranes, meconium staining, multiple births, maternal fever, and maternal anemia at delivery, were found to be associated with birth asphyxia.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was found in 32.14% of birth asphyxia cases, spontaneous vertex delivery in 44.39%, and instrumental delivery in 23.47%.
